name: run-hosted-morphic-runtime
problem_solved: execute one bounded deterministic target-neutral Morphic core through hosted, fake, and freestanding RISC-V execution boundaries
selection_reasons: The resource planner derives fixed storage and initialization order.
The scheduler owns target-neutral time and runnable ordering policy.
The event trace records normalized bounded behavior.
inherited_guarantees: Fixed resource derivation, stable runnable ordering, caller-controlled time, bounded trace storage, and explicit capacity failures.

One shared core owns planning, scheduling, tracing, and output formatting; hosted and fake machines provide bounded task output, while the freestanding RISC-V adapter adds only entry, stack, transport, shutdown, and panic behavior around the same shared execution path.
gaps_discovered: The hosted path still relies on Linux userspace. The freestanding riscv64 path now supplies explicit entry, stack/bootstrap, SBI output transport, shutdown, and panic behavior; trap handling, interrupts/timers, virtual-memory activation, broader hardware discovery, and Linux/POSIX/Alpine compatibility remain out of scope or unimplemented.
future_systems_enabled: later supervisor trap and machine-boundary work
